space: Avoid overcrowding inside the poultry house.
Provide enough space for chickens to move comfortably.
Space requirements depend on chicken type, age, and production system.
ventilation: Maintain good airflow inside the coop.
Ventilation should remove moisture, odor, and excess heat without creating strong drafts.
lighting: Provide appropriate lighting based on the age and purpose of the chickens.
Maintain a consistent lighting schedule when managing layers.

general: Provide feed appropriate for the chicken's age and production stage.
Keep feed clean and protected from moisture and contamination.
Avoid sudden major changes in feed whenever possible.
water: Provide continuous access to clean and fresh drinking water.
Monitor water consumption because changes may indicate management or health concerns.

generalMonitoring: Observe chickens daily for changes in activity, appetite, posture, and behavior.
Separate visibly sick birds from the flock when appropriate.
Keep records of unusual symptoms, mortality, and production changes.
warningSigns: Large drop in feed or water intake
health.guidance: SmartCoop AI provides general poultry management guidance and should not be treated as a confirmed veterinary diagnosis.

biosecurity: Limit unnecessary visitors inside poultry areas.
Avoid sharing contaminated equipment between poultry groups.
Control rodents, insects, and other possible disease carriers.
Keep new or returning birds separated before introducing them to an existing flock.
Maintain clean footwear and tools when entering poultry areas.
sanitation: Remove excessive manure and wet litter.
Regularly inspect the coop for moisture, pests, and damaged areas.
eggProduction: Egg production is affected by breed, age, nutrition, lighting, environment, and health.
Consistent access to feed and clean water supports stable production.
Sudden production decreases should be investigated together with changes in feed intake, health, lighting, and environment.
broilerManagement: Monitor growth, feed intake, water intake, and mortality.
Keep litter dry and feeders and drinkers accessible.
Use records to compare expenses, growth, and flock performance.
recordKeeping: Record chicken purchases and flock changes.
Record meat production or sales when applicable.
Review records regularly to identify changes in cost and production.
budgeting: Include chicken purchase cost, feed, housing materials, utilities, equipment, health-related expenses, and maintenance when estimating poultry expenses.
Use actual farm records whenever possible instead of relying only on estimates.
Compare expenses with production results when evaluating farm performance.

smartcoop.purpose: SmartCoop is a poultry planning and management system designed to assist users with poultry-related planning, recommendations, records, monitoring, and decision support.
